{{nihongo|'''Sumisaka Shrine'''|墨坂神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shinano Province]].

[[ja:墨坂神社 (須坂市)]]

{{wikidata link|Q85878507|ja|墨坂神社 (須坂市)|check_date=2026-05-26}}

== Japanese content ==
'''Sumisaka Shrine''' (すみさかじんじゃ) is the name of two shrines in {{ill|Suzaka, Nagano|Q850461|qid=Q850461}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Q127877|qid=Q127877}}. Both enshrine Sumisaka no Kami, and are said to have received one household of shrine allotment from the court in {{ill|Ten'ō|Q1373125|qid=Q1373125|lt=Ten'ō}} 1 (781) (from '{{ill|Shinshō Kyakuchokufushō|Q11502312|qid=Q11502312}}'). They are {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} of {{ill|Takai district|Q11668733|qid=Q11668733}} in {{ill|Shinano Province|Q289250|qid=Q289250}} listed in the '{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=register of deities}}.

=== Overview ===
*Nagano Prefecture, Suzaka City, Suzaka 1048 (Shibamiya), former kensha
*Nagano Prefecture, Suzaka City, Sumisaka 1-8-1 (Hachiman), former kensha

=== Shibamiya ===

|名称=Sumisaka Shrine (Shibamiya)

According to shrine tradition, it was founded in {{ill|Hakuhō|Q11580612|qid=Q11580612}} 2 ({{ill|647|Q31111|qid=Q31111}}) by soliciting the deity from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sumisaka Shrine}} in {{ill|Uda District, Nara|Q1131315|qid=Q1131315}}, {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}}. In addition to the main deity, {{ill|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata|Q9150391|qid=Q9150391|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto}} is enshrined. In the Edo period, the lords of {{ill|Suzaka Domain|Q585967|qid=Q585967}} actively donated shrine-building sites and other support. In Meiji 3 (1870), the shrine name was changed from Shibamiya to Sumisaka Shrine.

The annual festival is on September 14; in addition, the Oiyama Festival, Sericulture Festival, Iyasaka Festival, and Commerce/Industry Festival are held.

=== Hachiman ===
{{神社
|名称=Sumisaka Shrine (Hachiman)
|画像={{画像募集中|cat=須坂市}}
|所在地={{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Q127877|qid=Q127877}}{{ill|Suzaka, Nagano|Q850461|qid=Q850461}}Sumisaka 1-8
|位置={{Coord|36|39|4.1|N|138|18|7.2|E|display=inline}}
|祭神=Sumisaka Ōkami
|社格=former {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}}, {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}
|創建=
|本殿=
|例祭=September 22
|神事=
|地図={{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|36|39|4.1|N|138|18|7.2|E}}}}
}}
Founding is unknown. In addition to the main deity, it enshrines {{ill|Emperor Chūai|Q179971|qid=Q179971|lt=Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803|lt=Okinaga-tarashi-hime-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997|qid=Q317997|lt=Hondawake-no-Mikoto-no-Mikoto}}. A Shinto legal permit document from Keichō 2 (1597) remains for Oyama Village Sumisaka Shrine and Hachiman-gū. In the Edo period it received reverence from the lords of Suzaka Domain. In Kansei 2 (1790), the shrine name was changed from Hachiman-gū to Sumisaka Shrine.

The Sumisaka Shrine framed plaque dates from Kansei 2 (1790).

=== Alternative theory by Toshio Hoga ===
Hoga argues that this shrine, together with {{ill|Ikushimatarushima Shrine|Q11574513|qid=Q11574513}}, has the distinctive feature of appearing only in Kinai and Shinano Province, implying migration of central Kinai powerful clans that worshiped these two deities; he claims the worshiping clan was the {{ill|Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Q11595951|qid=Q11595951}}<ref>{{ill|Toshio Hōga|Q11452691|qid=Q11452691}}, "2. Early stage of the Nakatomi clan - diviners and ancestors of the Nakatomi," in 'Study of Ancient Clans 5: Nakatomi Clan, descendants of ancient diviners responsible for divination,' Aogaki Publishing, 2014, p.34.</ref>.
